name: Wayback Machine
summary: Queries the Internet Archive Wayback Machine for the capture history and archive availability of selected domains and URLs. Desktop only.
description:
Archive history for domains and URLs from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine: when a page was captured and what each capture was, or simply whether any capture exists. Both plugins run on Domain and URL nodes and need the desktop app.

## Plugins

Both take the node's `domain_name` (Domain, `infrastructure.domain`) or `url` (URL, `web.url`). A selected node without either is skipped and counted in the run summary.

### Wayback Snapshot History

`run.vineyard.plugins.wayback_snapshot_history`

- **Queries:** the Wayback CDX API for the captures of each selected node.
- **Adds:** one URL node (`web.url`) per capture, linked from the seed node by a `has archive` edge. Its `url` is the replay address `https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>/<original>`, and it carries `original_url`, `domain` (the host of the captured URL), `http_status` (the status recorded for the capture), `page_title` (`Wayback capture <timestamp>`), `final_url`, `wayback_timestamp`, `wayback_digest` and `wayback_mimetype`.
- **Parameters:**

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | Earliest capture date, `YYYYMMDD` | no lower bound |
| `to` | Latest capture date, `YYYYMMDD` | no upper bound |
| `limit` | Maximum captures per node, 1 to 500 | 50 |
| `drop_duplicates` | Keep only the newest capture of each content digest | on |

- The newest `limit` captures in the window are fetched, then written oldest first, so the result reads as a timeline.
- An identical digest is usually the same page crawled again rather than a change, so with `drop_duplicates` on the timeline keeps one capture per distinct content. Duplicates are dropped after `limit` is applied, so fewer than `limit` captures can be written. A capture without a digest is always kept.

### Wayback Availability

`run.vineyard.plugins.wayback_available`

- **Queries:** the Wayback Availability API for the closest capture of each selected node.
- **Adds:** properties on the selected node itself, and no nodes: `wayback_available` (true or false) and `wayback_checked_at`, plus `wayback_snapshot_url`, `wayback_snapshot_timestamp` and `wayback_snapshot_status` when a capture exists.
- A quick check of whether a page was archived at all, before asking for its history.

## Requirements

- **Desktop app only.** Neither web.archive.org nor archive.org sends CORS headers, so a browser cannot read their responses; the desktop app sends the requests from its main process. In the web app both plugins say so and stop.
- No API key or account, and no Vineyard-operated service.

## Cost and limits

- One request per selected node, for each plugin.
- Response bodies are capped at 4 MB for the CDX query and 64 KB for the availability check.
- If the archive answers 429 (rate limited), the run stops there and reports how many nodes it got through. A failed request or any other non-200 answer skips that node and the run moves on.

## What it contacts

- web.archive.org (CDX API) and archive.org (Availability API). The Internet Archive sees each domain or URL that is queried.
- Passive: the site behind the domain or URL is never contacted. Only the archive's records are read, and the archived pages themselves are not downloaded.
- Requests are anonymous, with no cookies or credentials, and do not follow redirects.

## Data and licences

Capture records come from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine. The replay URLs written to the graph point at the archived copies on web.archive.org.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-wayback-machine (Apache-2.0)

`dist/pack.mjs` is built from `src/` with a pinned esbuild, so the published bundle can be checked against the source: `node build.mjs && git diff --exit-code dist/pack.mjs`.

plugins.name: Wayback Snapshot History
plugins.description: Lists Wayback Machine captures of each selected Domain or URL and creates one URL node per capture (replay URL, original URL, HTTP status, timestamp, digest) linked "has archive" from the seed. Up to limit captures per node (default 50, max 500), filtered by the from/to and drop_duplicates params. Desktop only.

from.description: Earliest capture date, YYYYMMDD. Empty = no lower bound.

to.description: Latest capture date, YYYYMMDD. Empty = no upper bound.

limit.description: Maximum captures to fetch per node, 1–500. Default 50.

drop_duplicates.description: Keep only the newest capture of each content digest. On by default.

web_probe.purpose: Fetch the Wayback Machine capture history of each selected domain or URL.

plugins.name: Wayback Availability
plugins.description: Checks whether the Wayback Machine has a capture of each selected Domain or URL and writes the result on the node: wayback_available, plus wayback_snapshot_url, wayback_snapshot_timestamp and wayback_snapshot_status of the closest capture. Creates no nodes. Desktop only.

web_probe.purpose: Check whether the Wayback Machine has a capture of each selected domain or URL.
